gates.description: Every screen must have all five states: ideal, empty, loading, error, partial data
Responsive layouts must be defined for all breakpoints (mobile, tablet, desktop)
Color contrast must meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text)
All measurements must use design tokens, not hardcoded values
Accessibility specification must be attached (tab order, ARIA roles, keyboard shortcuts)
Interaction specifications must be documented (animations, transitions, timing)

anti_patterns.description: Spending hours on hover animations before validating the flow with users — polish is the last step
Designing for portfolio beauty instead of user effectiveness — gorgeous interfaces that fail usability tests
Designing only the ideal flow and ignoring errors, empty states, loading states, and edge cases
Creating custom components when platform patterns exist — every novel interaction is a cognitive tax on the user
Producing designs without engineering input and throwing them over the wall — constraints discovered too late
Designing with perfect data and perfect names — real data is messy: long names overflow, lists have 0 or 10,000 items

escalation_triggers: Requirements are ambiguous and PM is unable to clarify after two attempts
Engineering declares a designed interaction technically infeasible and no acceptable alternative exists
Accessibility requirements conflict with business requirements and PM insists on the inaccessible option
Design system lacks components for a critical pattern and there is no time to create them properly
User testing reveals a fundamental usability problem requiring architectural flow changes
Brand guidelines conflict with accessibility requirements (insufficient contrast, decorative fonts for body text)

input_requirements.description: PRD.md with feature requirements and user research findings

output_certifications: All five states designed for every screen (ideal, empty, loading, error, partial)
Responsive layouts defined for all breakpoints (mobile, tablet, desktop)
Color contrast meets WCAG AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 large text)
All measurements use design tokens, not hardcoded values
Accessibility specification attached (tab order, ARIA roles, keyboard shortcuts)
Interaction specifications documented (animations, transitions, timing, easing)
